finding.title: Close the DeviceRegistryDatabase connection on account_bootstrap.dart's exception path
finding.why: `registry.close()` sits at the end of the try block, not in a finally. If sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() (line 30) or registry.findById() (line 33) throws, execution jumps straight to the outer catch (line 51), which logs and returns a fallback filename WITHOUT ever closing the Drift-backed device_registry connection — the exact 'I/O fails halfway' scenario the Nygard lens asks about. Impact is low in practice (this runs once per app process at startup), but a leaked native database handle held for the app's whole lifetime is still an avoidable defect, and it would compound if this code path were ever retried (e.g. a future hot-reattempt) or re-used in a longer-lived context.
finding.recommendation: Move `final registry = ...` construction above a try/finally (or wrap the resolveActiveAccountId/findById calls in try{...}finally{ await registry.close(); }) so every exit path closes the connection.
acceptance_criteria: registry.close() executes on both the success path and any exception path out of bootstrapAccount.
A unit test makes sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() throw and asserts the registry/executor was still closed.

finding.title: Extract the repeated reorder-amnesty confirm-dialog preamble in the tracks reorder screens
finding.why: The same ~10-line block (fetch overdueCount, bail if unmounted, show ReorderConfirmDialog.showIfNeeded, bail if declined/unmounted) is copy-pasted 3 times across 2 files. A future change to the amnesty-guard contract has to be found and edited in 3 places; missing one leaves that screen silently skipping the guard.
finding.recommendation: Extract a shared helper (mixin or top-level function taking WidgetRef/BuildContext/CurriculumId) used by all three call sites.
acceptance_criteria: Single shared implementation; all three call sites delegate to it

finding.title: Replace the tautological AuthRepository mock-shape test in epic_25_schema_core_test.dart with real coverage or delete it
finding.why: The test stubs every AuthRepository member on a mocktail Mock and then asserts the mock returns exactly what it was just told to return — it can never fail regardless of what AuthRepositoryImpl actually does, so it gives false confidence that Story 25.11's 'sole firebase_auth consumer' AC is under test. Real behavioural coverage already exists separately in test/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl_test.dart, so today this test adds zero net verification while reading like acceptance coverage for the story.
finding.recommendation: Delete the runtime expect() calls and keep this as a documented compile-only shape check (a referenced-but-uncalled function is enough to prove the interface compiles), or point the docstring at auth_repository_impl_test.dart so reviewers don't mistake mock-echo assertions for behavioural coverage.
acceptance_criteria: test either exercises AuthRepositoryImpl directly or is reduced to a compile-time shape check with no expect() calls that only echo their own stubs

finding.title: Consolidate the tracks/{setup,stages,track_order} test suite onto mirrored paths under test/features/tracks/** (AG-5)
finding.why: test/features/track_setup/**, test/features/stages/**, and test/features/track_learning_order/** all still exist and DO test current lib code (confirmed via their imports) — they are not stale — but none of them mirror the actual lib/features/tracks/{setup,stages,track_order}/** layout. A correctly-mirrored tree has also grown alongside them (e.g. test/features/tracks/setup/**, test/features/tracks/track_order/**), so coverage for this feature area is now split across two parallel, differently-named directory trees. A developer adding a new test for goal_helpers.dart would not find the existing one unless they already knew to look under the legacy 'track_setup' (singular, no 'tracks/' prefix) name instead of the mirrored 'tracks/setup' path, risking either an undiscovered duplicate or accidentally-orphaned old tests.
finding.recommendation: Move test/features/track_setup/**, test/features/stages/**, and test/features/track_learning_order/** to their AG-5-mirrored locations under test/features/tracks/{setup,stages,track_order}/**, merging with the already-correct parallel tree where both exist for the same source file.
acceptance_criteria: AG-5's mirroring checker (once implemented) reports zero unmirrored test directories for tracks/setup, tracks/stages, and tracks/track_order.
No test file is lost or silently duplicated during the move (`flutter test` count before == after).

finding.title: Log the two silent catch blocks in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart via AppLogger
finding.why: Both catches swallow every exception with no AppLogger call. If programCalendarPositionProvider throws (line 430-431), overdueCount/todayDueCount silently become 0 — a falsely reassuring 'nothing overdue' on the dashboard per-track row — with zero breadcrumb to diagnose it. If getScopedContent throws inside _safeLoadLeavesForTrack (line 648), the track just vanishes from trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's output with no trace. The same file already fixes this exact anti-pattern under the F20 label for _safeLoadLeaves/_safeHeLabelLookup (lines ~570-609, which log via AppLogger.warning with event/fields/exception/stackTrace) — these two catches were never brought in line with that established, documented convention.
finding.recommendation: Log both catches via AppLogger.warning(event:, exception:, stackTrace:) before falling back, matching the F20 pattern used elsewhere in the same file.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch blocks call AppLogger before returning/defaulting
No 'catch (_) {' block in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart lacks an adjacent AppLogger call
